wd-q63382811.note: Station point (CC0), read 19 Nov 2026; not yet checked against the LINZ aerial.

genesis-nzx-fy26.title: Solid FY26 performance, strategy delivery continues at pace (NZX, 26 August 2026)
genesis-nzx-fy26.note: Huntly BESS stage 1 (100 MW / 200 MWh): commissioning under way, due to be fully operational by September 2026; stage 2 (100 MW / 200 MWh) reached FID, construction expected in FY27.

genesis-nzx-bess2.title: Genesis reaches FID on Second Stage Huntly BESS (NZX, 20 April 2026)
genesis-nzx-bess2.note: Stage 2: 100 MW / 200 MWh, ~NZ$106 million, FID 17 April 2026, commercial operation expected Q3 FY28; site total 200 MW / 400 MWh; shares stage 1's land, plant and grid connection; Saft supplies both stages; Genesis to own 100%.

essnews-huntly-2026.title: New Zealand brings 200 MWh grid-scale battery online (21 October 2026)
essnews-huntly-2026.note: Genesis has officially opened the 100 MW / 200 MWh Huntly battery: 70 Saft units installed by Northpower, about NZ$130 million, built in about 14 months, connected through Transpower's Huntly substation; up to 400 MW / 800 MWh planned at the site. Other reports date the opening 15 October 2026.

contact-glenbrook-battery.title: Glenbrook Ohurua Battery 1
contact-glenbrook-battery.note: NZ Steel's Glenbrook site, South Auckland; commissioned 2026; 100 MW (200 MWh); trading from 1 April 2026, opened 21 May 2026; 56 Tesla Megapack 2 XL units; land leased from NZ Steel; Battery 2 (200 MW) under way beside it.

contact-glenbrook-2026.title: Glenbrook Ohurua Battery officially opened (21 May 2026)
contact-glenbrook-2026.note: Opened 21 May 2026; 100 MW; $151 million; work started July 2024; NZ Steel leased land close to Auckland demand and transmission; 56 Tesla Megapack 2 XL; Battery 2 (200 MW, $235 million) online early 2028.

contact-glenbrook-2025.title: Major milestone reached for Contact's new grid-scale battery (11 April 2025)
contact-glenbrook-2025.note: Installation of 56 battery units begun at Glenbrook; on track to operate by March 2026; option to expand from 100 MW to 130 MW.

meridian-ruakaka-bess-2025.title: Completion of Ruakākā Battery Energy Storage System (NZX, 23 May 2025)
meridian-ruakaka-bess-2025.note: Construction complete and officially opened 23 May 2025, with final commissioning tests still to be approved; 100 MW / 200 MWh; within the $186 million budget; Saft the battery partner, Transpower in planning and commissioning; construction began Q1 2023; south of Whangārei; part of the Ruakākā Energy Park.

rnz-ruakaka-2025.title: Giant battery: first stage of Ruakākā Energy Park switched on (23 May 2025)
rnz-ruakaka-2025.note: 80 shipping-container-sized Saft batteries on two hectares at Marsden Point, beside the former oil refinery south of Whangārei; grid-connected since early 2025; to operate once final tests were signed off.

newpower-ea-2026.title: Submission on wholesale market arrangements for battery energy storage systems (30 June 2026)
newpower-ea-2026.publisher: NewPower Energy Services (published by the Electricity Authority)
newpower-ea-2026.note: NewPower Energy Limited is the owner, operator and trader of the Rotohiko BESS; NewPower's companies are subsidiaries of WEL Networks; Rotohiko is 35 MWh, at Huntly, connected to WEL Networks' distribution assets.

rnz-rotohiko-2023.title: WEL Networks opens first utility-scale battery (Nine To Noon, 31 October 2023)
rnz-rotohiko-2023.note: Battery near Huntly, 35 MWh, about 2,000 homes; WEL Networks set up NewPower Energy to own and operate it and sell into the reserves market.

ea-batteries-2024.title: Unlocking the potential for batteries to contribute to security of supply (16 April 2024)
ea-batteries-2024.note: The first grid-scale battery (35 MW, 35 MWh) was commissioned in 2023 by WEL Networks, near Huntly power station, and began charging and discharging into the grid in 2024.

ea-batteries-2026.title: Eye on electricity: battery performance in New Zealand (19 May 2026)
ea-batteries-2026.note: Rotohiko 35 MW / 35 MWh and Ruakākā 100 MW / 200 MWh have dispatched more often for instantaneous reserves than energy; Glenbrook-Ohurua 100 MW / 200 MWh recently commissioned; Genesis's Huntly 100 MW / 200 MWh due later in 2026.

seanz-mercury-tesla-2018.title: Mercury NZ picks Tesla for ground-breaking battery trial (24 January 2018)
seanz-mercury-tesla-2018.note: Mercury's release: a 1 MW / 2 MWh Tesla Powerpack 2 at Mercury's research and development centre in South Auckland, connected to the national grid; ready to trade in August 2018; over $2 million.

mercury-battery-2018.title: A Kiwi first: direct grid-connected battery is large and in-charge (news release, 22 August 2018)
mercury-battery-2018.note: Launched 22 August 2018 by the Minister of Energy: Mercury's Tesla Powerpack at its R&D centre in South Auckland, beside the grid's main route into Auckland; New Zealand's first directly grid-connected large-scale battery; nearly $3 million; a trial of trading and of working with Mercury's hydro and geothermal.

linz-aerial.title: LINZ aerial imagery (LINZ Basemaps)
linz-aerial.note: Aerial imagery (CC BY 4.0). We read station and substation points from it, 18 Nov 2026; the plant pages' aerial views come from it too.

transpower-assumptions-2026.title: TPM determination: Assumptions book v3.0 (30 June 2026)
transpower-assumptions-2026.note: Footnote 22: em6's KAW110 ONU value covers Onepu_KA24, TA2, TA3 and TOPP1 (SOSA: one 60 MW unit). Embedded generation table (p. 21): Waipori1A and Waipori2A unit 1 at HWB220, the other 2A units, 3 and 4 at BWK110 (para 113). Edgecumbe and Hawera modelled to retire in 2026 (Fonterra). Te Rere Hau repowering staged from 2029, before financial close. Appendix F (workbook on the same page, model inputs of 4 Jun 2026): existing plant capacities, thermal retirements, wind repowering, geothermal emission rates and committed projects.

transpower-appendix-d-2026.title: BBI Customer Allocation workbook, PY2026, adjustments up to 10 Nov 2026 (Assumptions Book Appendix D, updated 19 Nov 2026)
transpower-appendix-d-2026.note: Change log and one sheet per adjustment event (large plant connected or disconnected, changed point of connection, new customer), each with its effective date ('Allocation from') and the customer and grid exit point. Effective dates are for transmission charging, not necessarily first output or full commissioning.

linz-oio-202500586.title: Overseas Investment decision 202500586: Dannevirke SF Limited Partnership (27 Jan 2026)
linz-oio-202500586.publisher: Toitū Te Whenua LINZ (Overseas Investment Office)
linz-oio-202500586.note: Leasehold of about 37.4 ha at 440 Tamaki River Road, Dannevirke, for a solar farm of about 23 MWp; grazing continues; applicant 58% Australian, 42% New Zealand.

lightsourcebp-kowhai-opening.title: New Zealand: South Island's largest solar farm opens, supporting industrial electrification (15 Oct 2026)
lightsourcebp-kowhai-opening.note: 150 MWac and 168 MWdc; commissioning began in August 2026; officially opened on 15 October 2026; Synlait buys 25% of the output and Christchurch Airport buys under a long-term PPA; about 300,000 panels on 230 ha; 275 GWh a year expected.

lodestone-waiotahe.title: Te Herenga o Te Rā Solar Farm
lodestone-waiotahe.note: Read through search results (the site refuses automated reads). 42 MWp; first generation in December 2024 with commissioning work continuing in early 2025; 69 GWh a year when fully commissioned.

nzherald-pukenui-opening.title: Northland's new Pukenui Solar Farm to power 4000 homes after launch (16 Oct 2025)
nzherald-pukenui-opening.note: Officially opened in October 2025; around 35,000 panels on 17 ha on Lamb Rd; 20.8 MW; led by Aquila Clean Energy and Far North Solar Farm.

nzherald-ruakaka-construction.title: Meridian starts work on $227m Ruakākā solar farm to power Northland homes (2 Nov 2025)
nzherald-ruakaka-construction.note: 130 MW; ground broken in October 2025; about 250,000 panels on 201 ha across three sites; up to 230 GWh a year.

nzherald-ryman-solar-opening.title: On the up: Northland sun to power Ryman retirement villages New Zealand-wide (9 Dec 2025)
nzherald-ryman-solar-opening.note: The Ryman Healthcare Solar Farm (Papareireiā) at Maungatūroto was officially opened on 4 December 2025; about 32 GWh a year.

pvmag-lauriston-launch.title: JV partners launch New Zealand's largest solar farm (May 2025)
pvmag-lauriston-launch.note: 47 MW; more than 90,000 panels; up to 100 GWh a year; 10-year power purchase agreement with Genesis; Genesis and FRV Australia joint venture.

pvmag-pukenui-energised.title: Aquila, FNSF energise New Zealand solar farm (22 Oct 2025)
pvmag-pukenui-energised.note: Pukenui Solar Farm energised and commissioned; 35,000 PV panels on a 17 ha site near Pukenui.

pvmag-tauhei-energised.title: New Zealand's largest yet solar farm successfully energised (15 Jul 2026)
pvmag-tauhei-energised.note: Harmony Energy and Igneo Infrastructure Partners: the 150 MW Tauhei Solar Farm is energised and exporting; several months of testing and commissioning as output rises to the full plant capacity of 150 MW (202 MWp).

ryman-papareireia-live.title: Ryman Healthcare's sector-first solar farm officially goes live (5 Dec 2025)
ryman-papareireia-live.note: Officially went live on 4 December 2025; about 32 GWh a year; a sleeved power purchase agreement with Mercury supplements solar output when generation is low; joint venture of Tupu Tonu, Harbour Infrastructure and Purpose Capital (Maungatūroto Solar Farm Project LP).

meridian-ruakaka-energy-park.title: Ruakākā Energy Park (Meridian Energy project page)
meridian-ruakaka-energy-park.note: Solar farm (stage 2): 130 MW in the body (120 MW in the page's metadata), AC or DC not stated; about 250,000 panels on about 163 ha of the 201 ha site; construction from late 2025; up to 230 GWh a year; inverter stations and a 33 kV connection to a switching station at the battery site, then to Bream Bay. No first-generation or commissioning date given. Battery: 100 MW, 200 MWh, construction early 2023 to May 2025.

comcom-2025-nzcc-22.title: Genesis Energy, Contact Energy, Meridian Energy and Mercury NZ: authorisation final determination [2025] NZCC 22 (5 Nov 2025)
comcom-2025-nzcc-22.note: Three Rankine units at Huntly of 240 MW each; without the arrangements Genesis intended to retire Unit 2 in January 2026 (its certification expiring in February 2026); the Huntly Strategic Energy Reserve Huntly Firming Option, under which Mercury, Meridian and Contact contribute to Unit 2's costs, is authorised for 10 years to 31 December 2035.

auckland-otahuhu-heritage-2014.title: Otahuhu Historic Heritage Survey: overview report (final, August 2014)
auckland-otahuhu-heritage-2014.publisher: Auckland Council (Matthews & Matthews Architects and others)
auckland-otahuhu-heritage-2014.note: Section 4.4.3 Power (p. 54): the gas turbine station was built in the Baird's Road area and commissioned 1968–70, the first large gas turbine station in Australia and New Zealand; its turbines ran on fuel oil at first, and one was altered to burn natural gas from the Kapuni pipeline in 1971; two more turbines were added in 1977–78; it was reopened and returned to full operation during the 1992 power shortage; Otahuhu B opened in 2000.

nbr-fonterra-nova-2025.title: Fonterra to end Todd Corp gas deals in 2026 (29 Jan 2025)
nbr-fonterra-nova-2025.note: Read through search results (paywalled). Fonterra is ending its co-generation deals with Nova Energy in 2026; Nova supplies gas for Fonterra's 68 MW generation plant at Whareroa and its 10 MW plant at Edgecumbe.

fosters-projects.title: Projects
fosters-projects.note: Read through search results. Fonterra dairy factory, Edgecumbe: a 30 MW electrode boiler and a 4 MW resistive element boiler, with a building and water treatment plant; completion Q2 2026.

scoop-deep-stream-2005.title: Deep Stream Power for 3,100 Homes (15 Aug 2005)
scoop-deep-stream-2005.note: TrustPower's Deep Stream enhancement of its Waipori scheme: water from Deep Stream channelled to Lake Mahinerangi through a canal and head pond; two 2.5 MW units made surplus by the Coleridge upgrade; power for 3,100 homes by winter 2007.

engnz-waipori.title: Waipori Falls Hydro-electric Power Scheme
engnz-waipori.note: First station 1907 (two 1,000 kW alternators on Pelton wheels); two more dams and stations downstream in the 1950s; the original station replaced on a new site just upstream in the 1960s and 1970s; four stations on the Waipori River and two on Deep Stream, about 192 GWh a year.

manawa-kaimai-scheme.title: Kaimai Power Scheme
manawa-kaimai-scheme.note: Names the scheme's four stations: Lloyd Mandeno, Lower Mangapapa, Ruahihi and Kaimai 5; header says commissioned 1972, body says between 1972 and 1994; max 42.1 MW, about 169 GWh; no figures for single stations.

station_leads.name: Amethyst
station_leads.notes:
It can run islanded from the national grid

New Zealand Designed Six-Jet Vertical Pelton Turbine

The original 250 kW Amethyst Power Station, which was developed to supply the Harihari area, was commissioned in 1954 and decommissioned in 1991. It took water from the same river and was situated approximately 1 km upstream from the current site. Grade B (Westpower). Wikipedia 7.6 MW, 2013.

The Post (2 Oct 2026): nearing the end of its working life; NZ Windfarms' Oct 2024 documents said five turbines were not running and two ran at reduced capacity.
